QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_45

question.text: A Category II AIF wishes to enter the Dissolution Period to pursue the liquidation of its remaining 3 portfolio companies after the expiry of its 1-year Liquidation Period. What investor consent threshold is required to enter the Dissolution Period?

answer.text: Two-thirds by value (as for tenure extension).
75% of investors by value (consistent with the in-specie approval threshold).

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Chapter 12 and SEBI Circular dated April 26, 2024: A scheme shall enter a Dissolution Period only after receiving requisite consent from existing investors. In the absence of consent from 75% of investors, in-specie distribution rules apply (with the 25% bid / One Rupee fallback). The 75% threshold is the effective gate for the Dissolution Period route. **The Trap:** 51% and 2/3 are plausible but wrong in this context. Unanimous is not the standard. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers the 2024 amendments. Note the alignment of 75% threshold: wind-up (75%), in-specie (75%), Dissolution Period entry (75% alignment). These are the 'big three' 75%-by-value events on XIX-D. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Pre-solicit LP sentiment well before the Liquidation Period expiry. File the Information Memorandum with SEBI via a merchant banker with due-diligence certificate — this must be done BEFORE the Liquidation Period (or its extension) expires.
